name: Animal Handling
description: Care and use of animals, including raising, tending, grooming, and healing them. Specialties: falconry, specific animals.

name: Area Lore: {region}
description: Knowledge of one particular region, covenant, or even a village, including where things are in the immediate area, local history and legends, and the centers of power in the region. The smaller the region, the more detailed your knowledge. Specialties: geography, history, legends, politics, personalities.

name: Athletics
description: General physical prowess: moving smoothly, confidently, and with grace, and most large-muscle coordination. Specialties: acrobatics, contortions, grace, jumping, running.

name: Awareness
description: Noticing things, whether sought or unexpected, and staying alert in circumstances that require watchfulness. Specialties: bodyguarding, keeping watch, alertness, searching.

name: Bargain
description: Getting the greatest return for a service or product while paying the least, by reading the person you haggle with, knowing the general value of goods, and presenting yourself well. Specialties: specific types of products, hard sell.

name: Brawl
description: Fighting hand-to-hand without weapons, or with improvised weapons such as knives; also the Ability used to dodge attacks if you have no Martial Abilities. Specialties: punches, grapples, knives, dodging.

name: Carouse
description: Enjoying yourself without suffering adverse effects, such as drinking heavily without passing out, while staying familiar with acceptable behavior and balancing enjoyment with moderation. Lets a character have fun and make friends among the lower classes nearly anywhere, even among a different culture. Specialties: power drinking, drinking songs, games of chance, staying sober.

name: Charm
description: Enticing, fascinating, and endearing others to you on a personal basis; can be used to win someone over emotionally, especially romantically. Specialties: courtly love, first impressions, being witty.

name: Chirurgy
description: Middle Ages-style surgery used to help others recover from physical damage, encompassing tending and binding wounds of all varieties and cauterization. Specialties: cauterization, diagnosis, binding wounds, setting bones.

name: Concentration
description: Focusing your mental faculties on one task, particularly for extended periods, or when attempting a feat that demands extra attention or retrying after a failed action. Especially important for magi, since it helps them maintain concentration on spells despite distractions. Specialties: spell concentration, reading, lab work.

name: Craft: {craft}
description: Making things by hand in a specific trade; distinguished by the material worked with, though a Craft Ability can also cover working with several materials in one specific way. May be purchased more than once for different Crafts -- skill in one Craft does not imply skill in others. Specialties: as appropriate to the craft.

name: Etiquette
description: Knowing the social graces and how to behave in different situations; differs from Charm in that Etiquette covers proper behavior rather than charming behavior. Specialties: nobility, court, peasants, faeries, the Church.

name: Folk Ken
description: Understanding the background, personality, and motives of another person at a glance. Often rolled secretly by the storyguide, so the player doesn't know if the guess was correct or even botched. Specialties: peasants, townsfolk, nobles, clergy, magi, the opposite sex.

name: Guile
description: Telling convincing lies and feigning emotion, belief, or frame of mind; also covers disguising yourself and pretending to be something you are not. Often an opposed roll against the victim's Perception + Folk Ken or, for disguise, Perception + Awareness; understanding the target first grants a bonus. Specialties: particular sorts of deception, lying to authority, fast talk, elaborate lies.

name: Hunt
description: Setting snares, choosing appropriate hunting spots, and following and identifying the spoor of creatures of all varieties; also covers covering your tracks or not leaving any. Specialties: tracking, covering tracks, hunting a specific animal.

name: Intrigue
description: Dealing and plotting, including subtle use of power in non-confrontational ways; also covers negotiation, knowledge of formal and informal rules of conduct, and picking up information about those in power. A vital talent for those who frequent court or a Hermetic Tribunal. Specialties: gossip, plotting, rumormongering, alliances.

name: Judaic Lore
description: Knowledge of Jewish cultural practice as opposed to strictly religious detail, including poetry, folklore, and songs; all Jewish characters are versed in Judaic Lore to some degree. Specialties: folklore, music, poetry, songs.

name: Leadership
description: Getting people to obey your orders and follow you; can also be used to inspire fear in others, cowing them into submission. Specialties: intimidation, in combat, inspiration.

name: Legerdemain
description: Sleight of hand and confidence games requiring a delicate touch and hand-eye coordination, including filching from market stalls, cutting purses, picking locks, and the 'magical' trickery used to fleece credulous folk. Someone trying to spot the character's use of this Ability rolls Perception + Awareness (or their own Legerdemain, if any), with a +3 bonus for particularly delicate moves like picking pockets. Specialties: filching, picking pockets, 'magic' tricks.

name: Living Language: {language}
description: Fluency in a particular living language; when two people speak to each other, the lower Ability score determines how well they communicate, and related languages or dialects may carry a penalty at the storyguide's discretion. Characters are illiterate in the language unless they also have a score in Artes Liberales. Also covers artistic composition and storytelling in the language. Specialties: poetry, prose, specific dialects, expansive vocabulary, specific technical vocabulary, slang, storytelling.

name: Music
description: The ability to sing, play musical instruments, and compose new music. Specialties: sing, compose, any one instrument.

name: Mystery Cult Lore: {cult}
description: Knowledge of the legends, history, structure, operation, and goals of a particular Mystery Cult, including its magics, rites, secret passwords, and symbolism -- how to covertly signal membership and assess another's membership. Also covers the cult's ceremonies and, for a Mystagogue, guiding an Initiate through the Initiation Rites. Specialties: personalities, history, politics, one specific Initiation.

name: Organization Lore: {organization}
description: Knowledge of the legends, history, structure, operation, and goals of a specified organization, from as large as the Church to as small as a local craft guild -- the smaller the organization, the more detailed the knowledge. Order of Hermes Lore is particularly important to most magi. Specialties: personalities, history, politics.

name: Profession: {profession}
description: The ability to do a job that doesn't involve making something, such as jongleur, marshal, reeve, sailor, steward, teamster, or washerwoman. Specialties depend on the profession.

name: Ride
description: Riding and controlling a mount, especially under stress. Specialties: battle, speed, tricks.

name: Stealth
description: Sneaking about without being seen or heard, hiding in place, or following people without their noticing (rolled against the target's Perception). Specialties: hide, sneak, shadowing, urban areas, natural areas.

name: Survival
description: Finding food, water, shelter, a direct route, and relative safety in the wilderness, including mundane tasks like building a fire and cooking without implements. Specialties: specific locales.

name: Swim
description: Propelling yourself through water quickly and efficiently. Specialties: long distances, diving, underwater maneuvering.

name: Teaching
description: The ability to teach an Ability to someone else. Specialties: a particular Ability, particular kinds of student.

name: Art of Memory
description: The creation of memory palaces, a mnemonic technique in which you visualize a number of loci where you commit to memory a symbolic representation of a fact to be remembered; you have a number of loci equal to five times your score. To memorize a complex scene, image, or piece of writing you must succeed at a roll of Intelligence + Art of Memory against an Ease Factor set by the length or complexity of the item; on success you remember it in exact detail and may recall it at will, though it may take time to explore a locus. Characters without this Ability may memorize similar items with an Intelligence roll (with 3 extra botch dice) against the same Ease Factors, but must also repeat the roll to recall the memory perfectly, and lack the well-defined loci system. Specialties: an area of knowledge.

name: Artes Liberales
description: The seven liberal arts (the Trivium: grammar, logic, rhetoric; and the Quadrivium: arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, music) that form the basis of medieval higher education; it would be very rare for a character to have a score in any other Academic Ability without at least one point here. Also covers the ability to read and write: for every point in the Ability, the character can read and write one writing system, provided they know a language that normally uses it. Specialties: grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, music, Ritual magic, Ceremonial magic.

name: Civil and Canon Law
description: Civil Law is the law of the Roman Empire, the basis for most local legal systems and the law appealed to for international relations. Canon Law is the law of the Church, applying in all nations and governing church workings and some other areas such as marriage; clergy are subject only to Canon Law, not customary or Civil Law. This Ability covers knowledge of both. Other religions, particularly Judaism and Islam, have their own separate versions of this Ability. Specialties: laws and customs of a specific area, papal laws.

name: Common Law
description: Knowledge of the laws of England. There is no auctor for this Ability, and it is only taught in England. Specialties: local laws, exchequer laws.

name: Dead Language: {language}
description: Reading and writing a language no longer in common speech, available only to educated characters; the most important example is Latin, the language of formal education, the Church, and the Order of Hermes, with Arabic, Greek, and Hebrew filling similar roles elsewhere. Specialties: academic usage, Church ceremonies, Hermetic usage.

name: Islamic Law
description: The Muslim version of Civil and Canon Law; the major sources are the Qur'an and the Sunna. Specialties: any one of the sources of Islamic Law, particular topics, customs of a particular area.

name: Medicine
description: The formal study of the body and its diseases, based on the theory of the four humors, whose imbalance causes illness (hence practices like bloodletting). Also covers treating poisons and starvation, but not wounds (see Chirurgy). Specialties: anatomy, apothecary, physician.

name: Philosophiae
description: The study of natural philosophy, moral philosophy, and metaphysics, all with Aristotle as the auctor; studied after the Arts but before Law, Theology, or Medicine. Specialties: natural philosophy, moral philosophy, metaphysics, Ritual magic, Ceremonial magic.

name: Rabbinic Law
description: The Jewish version of Civil and Canon Law; the major sources are the Talmud, the Oral Torah, and the Responsa of the Geonim. Specialties: any one of the sources of Rabbinic Law, dietary laws, particular topics, precedents of a given area.

name: Theology: Christian
description: The study of God and his work in the world, with the Bible and Peter the Lombard's Sententiae as the auctores; theological speculation is abstruse, and many theologians face (and sometimes overturn) accusations of heresy. Specialties: biblical knowledge, heresy, history.

name: Theology: Islam
description: The Islamic equivalent of Theology: Christian; the major sources are the Qur'an and the Sunna. Specialties: the Qur'an, debates, history, prophets.

name: Theology: Judaism
description: The Jewish equivalent of Theology: Christian; the major sources are the Torah, the Nevi'im, and the Kutuvim. Specialties: the Torah, creation, history, prophecies.

name: Bows
description: Using bows and arrows. Specialties: any one weapon.

name: Great Weapon
description: Fighting with a weapon that requires two hands to use. Specialties: any one weapon.

name: Single Weapon
description: Fighting with a weapon used in one hand, possibly with a shield in the other; includes lances used from horseback. Specialties: any one weapon or shield, covering that weapon with any shield or none, and that shield with any weapon.

name: Thrown Weapon
description: Fighting at range using weapons which are thrown. Specialties: any one weapon.

name: Code of Hermes
description: Judging events according to the Code of Hermes and the Peripheral Code, including memorized precedents and the practical side of enforcing Hermetic law, such as knowing when to push for a vote or how to present an argument. Specialties: Wizards' Marches, apprentices, mundane relations, Tribunal procedures, political intrigue.

name: Dominion Lore
description: Knowledge of the manifestations of the power of the Divine -- miracles rather than politics (unlike Church Lore) and power rather than doctrine (unlike Theology). Specialties: angels, saints, Divine creatures.

name: Enigmatic Wisdom
description: The understanding Criamon magi have of the Enigma; described in the Hermetic Magic chapter. Cannot be learned by non-Criamon characters, even with access to Arcane Abilities.

name: Faerie Lore
description: Familiarity with faerie powers, weaknesses, motivations, and areas. Specialties: faerie forests, faerie mounds, specific types of faeries.

name: Faerie Magic
description: The connection to the power of the Faerie realm possessed by Merinita magi; cannot be learned by other characters, even with access to Arcane Abilities. Described in the Hermetic Magic chapter.

name: Finesse
description: Manipulating your spells and performing special feats with them, such as positioning objects delicately or precisely targeting spells. Specialties: grace, precision, any one Form.

name: Heartbeast
description: The ability shared by all Bjornaer magi to take the form of their heartbeast; cannot be learned by non-Bjornaer characters, even with access to Arcane Abilities. Described in the Hermetic Magic chapter.

name: Infernal Lore
description: Understanding and familiarity with the Infernal and its agents, including demons and undead and their habits and weaknesses, and the power of curses. Specialties: demons, undead, curses.

name: Magic Lore
description: Knowledge of magical creatures, areas, and traditions. Specialties: creatures, magical traditions, regiones.

name: Magic Theory
description: Knowledge of what magic is and how it works, used primarily in the laboratory for inventing spells and enchanting items; distinct from Magic Lore, which covers magical things in general rather than technical Hermetic theory. Anyone can learn it given a teacher or book, but it is of little use to those without The Gift. Specialties: inventing spells, enchanting items, a single Art.

name: Parma Magica
description: The Hermetic ritual of magic resistance: a two-minute ritual that adds five times your Parma Magica score to your Magic Resistance until the next sunrise or sunset, whichever comes first, and can be temporarily suppressed by concentrating. You may also extend protection to one other consenting person per point of Parma Magica by touch, for as long as either can see the other, at a cost of 3 points to your own effective score while protecting others. Only Gifted characters can learn it, and only Hermetic magi actually know it -- the Order enforces 'Join or Die' on anyone else who learns it. Specialties: protection from any specific Form.

name: Penetration
description: Getting your spell through a target's Magic Resistance. Specialties: any one Art.

name: Animal Ken
description: You can communicate with animals as if they were human beings. Treat your score in Animal Ken as your score in a language the animal speaks fluently, and you can use Animal Handling as a substitute for any social Ability affecting humans. Has no effect on the attitude of animals to you, or you to animals, and other people cannot understand your communication with the animals. Specialties: a particular type of animal, a particular type of communication.

name: Corpse Magic
description: Temporarily revives a corpse that has not received burial rites from a Divinely-sanctioned religion and is relatively intact (at minimum a spine, a skull, and more than half its long bones); it takes fifteen minutes of chanting to awaken the dead. The caster generates a Casting Total (Communication + Corpse Magic + Aura modifier + stress die) compared against Ease Factors to determine what the corpse can be made to do, from merely speaking to being animated and placed under direct mental control; commanding an animated corpse uses a Communication + Leadership roll, and the character must know the language the corpse spoke in life. Animated corpses typically have a Magic Might of 9, which the Corpse Magic's Penetration Total must exceed to raise them from the grave. Specialties: kings, soldiers, compelling truth, animating the dead.

name: Crafter's Healing
description: Treats a wound, once per wound regardless of severity, with a Presence + Crafter's Healing roll against the Ease Factor for improving that wound's recovery; success heals the wound one level (heavy to medium, medium to light, light to healed), at a cost of a Long-Term Fatigue level. A failed roll wastes the fatigue for no effect; a botch inflicts a similar wound on the healer. The recipient gains a Warping Point each time this Ability is used on them, win or lose. Specialties: particular kinds of wounds.

name: Curse-Throwing
description: Heals diseases, removes curses, and dispels detrimental magical effects by transferring their effects to another person via an elaborate ritual -- a charm combining a physical object and a repeated chant, touched to both target and recipient (or an Arcane Connection to the recipient). Cannot affect Flaws such as Lesser or Greater Malediction, but can transfer other curses, diseases, or harmful magical effects; if either party has Magic Resistance, the caster's Penetration Total must exceed it. A botch swaps the curse onto the caster instead. Specialties: diseases, faerie curses, livestock.

name: Dowsing
description: Finding things nearby using a dowsing rod and intuitive sense: concentrate on the thing sought, hold the rod out, and follow its motions to the target. Finding something specific requires an appropriate sympathetic connection to it. The searcher must designate the search area in advance -- if the item isn't present, the attempt automatically fails -- and the time required depends on the size of the area. Specialties: searching for a particular kind of thing, searching in a particular kind of place.

name: Embitterment
description: Causes one person to hate another; described in the Hermetic Magic chapter.

name: Enchanting: {performance}
description: Influencing others through a particular performance Ability. A specific effect requires words the audience can understand; general effects work on animals, but specific effects only work on creatures that understand words. Roll Communication + Enchanting Ability against an Ease Factor set by the desired effect -- calming, winning love, inciting a riot, or greater feats -- and Penetrate Magic Resistance if the target has any. A botched roll produces an unwanted emotion instead. Specialties: a particular emotion, a particular sort of person.

name: Entrancement
description: Controls another's will: by holding eye contact for several seconds and speaking a verbal command, roll Presence + Entrancement against the target's Stamina, with a possible bonus for the victim depending on how dangerous or objectionable the command is. Hermetic magi resist with their normal Mentem Magic Resistance. The blind and those with closed eyes are immune, and a victim cannot look away unless they win the opposed roll. Specialties: a specific sort of command, a specific sort of person.

name: Font of Knowledge
description: Lets a creature attempt a task with any untrained Ability as if it possessed a score of 2, by succeeding at an Intelligence + Font of Knowledge roll against an Ease Factor that rises with repeated use in a day (failed attempts still count toward the daily total). Specialties: a particular topic.

name: Hex
description: Brings injury or ruin on an enemy: activated by making eye contact and declaring your purpose aloud, by tracing occult signs and symbols on the target, or via an Arcane Connection and a representation that channels the effect through sympathetic magic, always with a physical component such as tying knots or the evil eye. The caster states a time frame for the effect (from immediate to generational -- sooner manifestations are weaker, longer delays more potent) and rolls Intelligence + Hex + aura bonus + delay modifier against an Ease Factor to determine severity, from a minor mishap up to sudden death. A botch may misfire onto the caster or someone close to her instead. Victims can undo a hex through Divine absolution or other supernatural remedies. Specialties: a specific duration, one method of hexing, a particular effect.

name: Induction
description: Creates illusions visible only to the target's mind; each attempt requires talking to the victim for at least a minute, and characters who cannot hear the inducer are immune. Roll Communication + Induction against an Ease Factor set by how risky the illusion is to believe, not its complexity -- the victim remains dimly aware of reality and can snap out of it if threatened. A successful inducer can spend more time to escalate the risk level further. Specialties: particular kinds of illusion.

name: Magic Sensitivity
description: Lets you identify a place or object as magical, at the cost of subtracting your Magic Sensitivity score from your own Magic Resistance. Roll Perception + Magic Sensitivity against an Ease Factor the storyguide sets based on what's being detected -- an aura, an active spell or enchanted item, or a magical creature's Might. Specialties: auras, magical creatures, enchanted items, active spells.

name: Persona
description: Lets you alter your appearance to adopt a different identity -- hair and eye color, complexion, build, height within your Size, apparent age, even gender -- total changes proof against even intimate scrutiny, though your Characteristics, Virtues, and Flaws remain unchanged. Adopting or shedding an identity takes a round of concentration and a Stamina + Persona roll against an Ease Factor of 9. You gain one identity per point of Persona, and must design a new one each time the Ability increases. Specialties: priests, peasants, magi.

name: Premonitions
description: An intuitive sense that something is wrong or likely to go wrong soon; roll Perception + Premonitions against an Ease Factor set by the imminence and severity of the danger. Beating the Ease Factor by 3 or more also grants some sense of the danger's nature, with more detail the higher the roll. Specialties: threats to a particular person or group of people, particular kinds of threats.

name: Second Sight
description: Lets you see through illusionary concealment and disguise, including invisibility, and see naturally invisible things such as spirits and the boundaries between regio levels. The Ease Factor to see through concealment is usually 6 plus the magnitude of the effect or the responsible creature's Might; seeing a naturally invisible thing is usually Ease Factor 9. Does not let you see a creature's or spell's true underlying form if it has actually been transformed. Specialties: regiones, invisible things, illusory disguises, faeries, ghosts.

name: Sense Holiness and Unholiness
description: Lets you feel the presence of good and evil: a Perception + Sense Holiness and Unholiness roll against an Ease Factor of 9 senses holiness or unholiness in a general area, or 15 in a specific person or object; detecting a demon's true nature normally succeeds automatically (though its Magic Resistance must still be Penetrated), while a divine being actively hiding its nature raises the Ease Factor to 15. This Ability is granted by the Divine realm rather than Magic or Faerie. Specialties: good or evil.

name: Sense Passions
description: Senses the personality and desires of an intelligent being by reading the tarnish on its soul: a Perception + Sense Passions roll against an Ease Factor of 9 senses the target's most powerful current emotion, or 15 identifies their most dominant Personality Trait; a 12 or better also lets you pick out the strongest source of emotion in the general area. The effect must Penetrate the target's Magic Resistance if any, and can also detect nearby incorporeal spirits and sense whether an aura carries Divine or Infernal tarnish or temper, though it cannot distinguish which. Specialties: auras, emotions, Personality Traits, in a general area.

name: Shapeshifter
description: Lets you change your shape into that of a mundane animal, from the size of a robin to that of a bear; requires a round of concentration and a Stamina + Shapeshifter roll against an Ease Factor of 9, both to change and to change back. You have a limited repertoire of shapes, one per point of the Ability, and may choose a new one each time it increases. Specialties: one of your shapes, particular conditions for the change.

name: Summon Animals
description: Summons animals; described in the Hermetic Magic chapter.

name: Whistle Up The Wind
description: Creates wind by whistling; described in the Hermetic Magic chapter.

name: Wilderness Sense
description: A mystical attunement to the ways of the wilderness: a Perception + Wilderness Sense roll against an Ease Factor of 9 reveals the direction of north, the upcoming weather, or the presence of natural hazards or resources -- one roll reveals only one piece of information. Specialties: direction, weather, hazards, resources.
